# Builds-on declaration (v1)

Schema for `.tera/builds-on/<installation>.hcl` declarations per [ADR-158](../adr/ADR-158-building-on-a-plugin.md) D1. A **builds-on declaration** is a vault saying which major version of an installed plugin it builds on: `builds_on "kb" { major_version = "v2" }` says this vault's recipes are written against major version `v2` of the installation `kb`. A repository's commit therefore says what it builds on, one small file per plugin.

**The file stem is the installation's name**, so `kb.hcl` declares what the vault builds on of the installation `kb` — the name the deployment installed it under, which is not necessarily the plugin's own (ADR-156 D5). One file per installation is what keeps a vault from declaring two major versions of one plugin. The recipe declares a single `builds_on` block whose label is optional and, if written, must equal that stem.

**`major_version` is a major token**: `v<N>` for a plugin at 1.0 or later (`v2`), or `v0.<m>` before 1.0 (`v0.3`), exactly as a release's major is derived from its semver `version` (ADR-157 D3). Any other spelling — `2`, `v2.1`, `V2` — is refused at load naming the file, because a declaration whose major no release can derive can never resolve.

**Any vault may declare**, the system vault included. Outside the system vault the directory is the contribute ability `vaults/contribute/builds-on`, which the `repository` role the binary contributes grants. A plugin does not declare in its vault: it declares in its manifest, so a plugin vault carrying `.tera/builds-on/` is refused by its allow-list.

A declaration is loaded and checked for spelling only. Whether the installation it names is installed, and whether that installation provides the major, is not decided at load: a declaration naming either loads without refusal.

## Example

A minimal `builds-on`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/builds-on/example-builds-on.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

builds_on "example-builds-on" {
  major_version = "v2"
}
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | string | yes | — | — | const `v1` | Per-recipe grammar version. Required; this schema applies when version is v1. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | The name of the installation built on (the HCL block label). Optional: the filename stem is the identity, so a label, if written, must equal it. It is an installation name: lower-case letters, digits and -, starting with a letter or digit. |
| `major_version` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | The major version of the installation this vault builds on: v<N> for a plugin at 1.0 or later (v2), or v0.<m> before 1.0 (v0.3), each number without a leading zero. It is spelled as a release's major is derived from its semver version (ADR-157 D3), and any other spelling (2, v2.1, V2) is refused at load. Whether the installation provides this major is not decided at load. |
